summary: The core run executed and refuted the narrow claim, so that account is corrected. Receipt 9a8b2864badf41a183a56bcfe91e49a2 (exit 101) parsed two events: `lost_accepted_window` shows dropped=Accepted:1, follower_accepted_idx=1, accept_decide_total=1 — no new client proposal in the whole 500-step window — yet leader_decided_idx=1 and follower_decided_idx=1, with produced=BLE:676,Prepare:4,Promise:6,AcceptSync:6,AcceptDecide:1,Accepted:3,PrepareReq:2,Decide:1. Three Accepted replies from a single AcceptDecide point at the accept-sync path (handle_acceptsync pushes a fresh Accepted with the follower's current index, follower.rs:53-79) reached after a new Prepare/Promise cycle, so the acceptance is re-advertised through ballot-change/re-sync paths even though the Accept-phase resend arms really are empty. The question is now conclusion explained with defect_claim refuted, and the counter-limitation is kept: that churn may be an artifact of the previous harness cadence, so whether a lost Accepted is repaired without any ballot change stays a necessary gap. The control's failure in the same run is attributed to the probe, not the target (it read the follower's decided index before the Decide was delivered). A revised experiment was requested: per-node tick-and-deliver cadence, post-drop wire tracing, an environment-only assertion (exactly one AcceptDecide) and 20 extra control steps — a measurement of the repair path rather than a prediction. Not locally compiled: rustfmt is unavailable and the omnipaxos test-target build (kompact and friends) exceeds my local window, so the executed receipt decides.
